walkthroughs.body_html:
Independent Investigation (NEA) — a core area of A-Level Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Independent Investigation (NEA) brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Independent Investigation (NEA).

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between primary and secondary data in geography fieldwork?
options: Refugees come from war zones and economic migrants come from rich countries.
Primary data is collected in primary schools and secondary data in secondary schools.
Primary data is more important and secondary data is less reliable.
Primary data is collected first-hand by the researcher (surveys, measurements, observations); secondary data already exists and is found in sources (census data, maps, published reports).

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a refugee and an economic migrant?
options: Refugees come from war zones and economic migrants come from rich countries.
Refugees and economic migrants are basically the same thing.
FDI is when individuals send money home to their families abroad.
A refugee is forced to flee due to persecution, war or disaster and has legal protections under international law; an economic migrant chooses to move primarily for work or better living standards.
